source:
Farah: The shelter program is over budget. We approved $3.9M for FY25 and the ledger shows $4.62M spent through Q3, which is 118% of the full-year figure with a quarter still to go.
Gus: It is not over budget. The $4.62M includes $810,000 of pass-through county reimbursement that lands in the same cost center. Net of that, spend is $3.81M, or 97.7% of the approved amount.
Farah: The reimbursement has not been received. The county has paid $290,000 of the $810,000 and the rest is an invoice, not cash.
Gus: The invoice is due in 30 days and the county has never missed one. Booking it as spend when it is owed back to us is what makes the number look like 118%.
Farah: Until the $520,000 arrives, we are carrying it. If it slips into FY26 the program has spent 105% of its budget in FY25 whatever the ledger says.
Gus: And if it arrives on time, which it will, we are under budget by $90,000. The only question is whether you count receivables.

extraction.mainQuestion: Is the shelter program over its FY25 budget?

positions.label: The program is over budget
positions.thesis: Gross spend of $4.62M against a $3.9M budget means the program is over budget until the outstanding $520,000 reimbursement is actually received.
positions.steelman: A receivable is a promise, not money; while the town is carrying $520,000 of unpaid county invoice, the program has consumed more than it was given.

groundingQuotes.quote: The shelter program is over budget.
Until the $520,000 arrives, we are carrying it.

positions.label: The program is within budget
positions.thesis: Net of $810,000 in county reimbursement, spend is $3.81M, which is 97.7% of the approved amount and under budget.
positions.steelman: Pass-through reimbursement is owed back by a county that has never missed an invoice; counting it as spend double-counts money that was never the program's cost.

groundingQuotes.quote: Net of that, spend is $3.81M, or 97.7% of the approved amount.
